overview.headline: Plutonium isotopes, half-life, decay and reactor fuel cycle

keyPoints.point: Plutonium is created in a reactor when uranium atoms absorb neutrons to form new material
keyPoints.quote: Plutonium is created in a reactor when uranium atoms absorb neutrons.

keyPoints.point: five common isotopes of plutonium are fissionable when struck by a neutron
keyPoints.quote: There are five “common” isotopes of plutonium, Pu-238, Pu-239, Pu-240, Pu-241, and Pu-242.

keyPoints.point: half-life values differ in years and shorter half-lives decay more quickly
keyPoints.quote: Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241’s half-life is 14.4 years.

keyPoints.point: Plutonium isotopes transform when they decay into different isotopes or elements such as uranium and daughter products
keyPoints.quote: Like any radioactive isotopes, plutonium isotopes transform when they decay.

keyPoints.point: Reprocessing uses chemicals to separate plutonium from uranium and other fission products to make MOX fuel
keyPoints.quote: This process, known as reprocessing, uses chemicals to separate plutonium from uranium and other fission products.

keyTerms.gloss: type of radiation that is easily stopped and has short range
keyTerms.quote: Plutonium predominantly emits alpha particles – a type of radiation that is easily stopped and has a short range.

keyTerms.gloss: atom nucleus can easily split apart when struck by neutron
keyTerms.quote: These are all “fissionable” – the atom’s nucleus can easily split apart if it is struck by a neutron.

keyTerms.gloss: time span in years for half of radioactivity to be lost
keyTerms.quote: Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241’s half-life is 14.4 years.

keyTerms.gloss: radioactive materials formed from decay that are themselves radioactive
keyTerms.quote: Many of these “daughter products” are themselves radioactive.

keyTerms.gloss: process using chemicals to separate plutonium from uranium and fission products
keyTerms.quote: This process, known as reprocessing, uses chemicals to separate plutonium from uranium and other fission products.

keyTerms.gloss: mixed oxide fuel made by mixing plutonium oxide with uranium oxide
keyTerms.quote: Once separated, plutonium oxide can be mixed with uranium oxide to produce mixed oxide or MOX fuel.
